name_reason: Name already correct and compliant: data_fd2_ prefix, battle core-table domain, descriptor 'map_height_tiles' precisely reflects semantics and data shape (a tile count). Confirmed by both writers (fd2_load_chapter_battle_data @0x10932 and fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @0x1022e) reading the second 16-bit field of the FDFIELD.DAT tile-map header: data_fd2_battle_map_height_tiles = (int)*(short *)(_battle_tile_map + 2), companion to width @0x53AC1 = *(short *)_battle_tile_map. Readers use it as the y-axis bottom-edge / row limit (cursor clamp 'height - 1' in fd2_cursor_move_down; scroll check 'height - window_max_y' in fd2_walk_step_down). No Ghidra address residue in the name; no domain ID to preserve.
purpose: Height (in tiles) of the current battle map; the y-axis bottom-edge / row-count limit used to clamp the cursor and gate vertical scrolling of the tile-grid viewport.
logic_summary: BSS zero-init uint32 scalar. Set at chapter-load (fd2_load_chapter_battle_data) and save-load (fd2_load_save_and_init_engine) by sign-extending the second 16-bit field of the decrypted FDFIELD.DAT tile-map header (offset +2) into a 32-bit slot; companion data_fd2_battle_map_width_tiles is the first field (offset +0). Consumed read-only by ~17 callers across cursor movement, walk-step animation, AoE/target scanning, tactical overview zoom, and scaled tile-map blitting as the vertical (row) traversal limit (e.g. height-1 cursor clamp, height-window_max_y scroll trigger).
datatype: uint32 (32-bit dword; source field is a signed 16-bit value sign-extended on load)
element_semantics: Single scalar: number of tile rows in the current battle map (small positive integer). Highest valid tile y-coordinate is height-1.
comment_original_issue: src comment was accurate except it described consumers as using the value as the 'column count / bottom-edge limit'; for the height global that is the row count / y-axis bottom-edge limit (column count is the width companion). Corrected the phrase; rest of the block (companion, both writers, MOVSX-signed widen, ~17 readers, 'height - 1' cursor clamp, BSS zero-init) was verified correct.
notes: Data address (not a function): get_plate_comment returned 'No function at address' as expected; read existing PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline (was null) and created a concise data plate via cu.setComment(CodeUnit.PLATE_COMMENT, ...). src comment edited surgically via Edit (single phrase). No rename applied (name_verdict=keep). No logic/type/declaration changed.
